context.analysis:
## Overview
This system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations to approve, decline, or flag suspicious transactions. It maintains PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while supporting low-latency decision-making and human case management.

## Key Elements
* **Payment Merchants / End Consumers**: External users initiating transactions.
* **Fraud Analysts & Risk/Compliance Officers**: Internal personnel reviewing flagged cases and ensuring regulatory compliance.
* **Risk / Data Scientists**: Internal users updating fraud rules and ML models.
* **Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System**: Core AWS-hosted system processing authorizations and case reviews.
* **Payment Gateway / Acquirer**: External system submitting authorization requests.
* **Card Networks / Tokenization Vault**: External provider supplying tokenized card data.
* **Identity Provider (IdP)**: External system managing OAuth2/SAML authentication.

## Relationships
* **Payment Gateway -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System**: HTTPS / gRPC for real-time authorization requests.
* **Fraud Analysts -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System**: HTTPS via TLS 1.3 for the Case Management UI.
* **Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System -> Tokenization Vault / IdP**: HTTPS via mTLS for token resolution and authentication.
* **Risk / Data Scientists -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System**: HTTPS / AWS IAM for secure model and rule artifact deployment.

## Technology Stack
* **AWS**: Cloud provider hosting containerized workloads within budget constraints.
* **AWS ECS**: Container orchestration for running scalable screening services.
* **ONNX Runtime / TorchScript**: Embedded model runtimes for low-latency ML inference.
* **AWS S3 Object Lock**: WORM-configured storage ensuring tamper-evident, 7-year audit logging.
* **Redis**: In-memory caching for feature stores using AWS KMS encryption.

## Rationale
The architecture prioritizes sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS by embedding lightweight inference runtimes and utilizing optimized AWS container infrastructure. Security controls like tokenization and WORM storage ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and immutable auditing within budget and team limits.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform deployed on AWS that evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to approve, decline, or flag suspicious transactions while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.]
[Its core purpose is to deliver sub-50ms fraud decisions at scale, support fraud analysts with secure case management, and ensure tamper-evident 7-year auditability within a fixed budget.]

## Key Elements
* API Gateway / Ingress Container (AWS API Gateway or Envoy)
* Fraud Scoring Engine Container (Go or Rust)
* Case Management Container (Node.js/Python + React SPA on Amazon S3 / CloudFront)
* Model Registry Container (MLflow on Amazon ECS)
* Database & Storage (Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 with append-only tables and immutable triggers)
* Caching Layer (Amazon ElastiCache with Redis OSS)
* External Systems: Payment Gateway / Acquirer, Card Networks / Tokenization Vault, Identity Provider (IdP)
* Personas: Payment Merchants / End Consumers, Fraud Analysts & Risk/Compliance Officers, Risk / Data Scientists

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> API Gateway / Ingress Container (HTTPS / gRPC)
* Fraud Analysts & Risk/Compliance Officers -> Case Management Container (HTTPS via TLS 1.3)
* API Gateway / Ingress Container -> Card Networks / Tokenization Vault (HTTPS via mTLS)
* All internal containers -> Identity Provider (IdP) (HTTPS via mTLS / OAuth2/SAML)
* Inter-container communication (API Gateway to Fraud Scoring Engine) -> gRPC over AWS VPC internal networks via mTLS

## Technology Stack
* Cloud Infrastructure: AWS (Region: eu-west-1) managed via Amazon ECS (Fargate) for minimal operational overhead.
* Core Scoring Language: Go or Rust for the Fraud Scoring Engine to guarantee P99 latency below 50ms at 3,000 TPS.
* Persistence & Audit: Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 with append-only tables and immutable cryptographic triggers for R-06 tamper-evident 7-year audit logs.
* Caching: Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) for low-latency feature lookups and rate limiting.
* Model Management: MLflow on Amazon ECS for zero-downtime model and rule updates via S3 memory caching.
* Security & Observability: AWS IAM Roles for Tasks, AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Private CA for mTLS rotation, and distributed tracing via AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry.

## Rationale
[This architecture uses managed AWS services like ECS Fargate and Aurora Serverless v2 to minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team while strictly staying under the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]
[It guarantees high availability, sub-50ms P99 latency, and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance through in-memory caching, boundary tokenization, and immutable audit logging.]

Fraud Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to approve, decline, or flag suspicious transactions while ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It delivers sub-50ms fraud decisions and provides comprehensive auditability for compliance officers.

## Key Elements
- Ingress Router Component (Go/Rust)
- Feature Aggregator Component (Go/Rust)
- Execution & Scoring Component (Go/Rust)
- Audit & Persistence Dispatcher Component (Go/Rust)
- Fallback Circuit Breaker Component (Go/Rust)
- API Gateway / Ingress Container (AWS API Gateway or Envoy)
- Fraud Scoring Engine Container (Go or Rust)
- Case Management Container (Node.js/Python + React SPA on Amazon S3 / CloudFront)
- Model Registry Container (MLflow on Amazon ECS)
- Database & Storage (Amazon Aurora Serverless v2)
- Caching Layer (Amazon ElastiCache with Redis OSS)

## Relationships
- API Gateway / Ingress Container -> Fraud Scoring Engine Container [gRPC over AWS VPC internal networks via mTLS]
- Fraud Scoring Engine Container -> Caching Layer [Redis OSS Protocol over TLS]
- Fraud Scoring Engine Container -> Database & Storage [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol via AWS IAM authentication]
- Model Registry Container -> Fraud Scoring Engine Container [S3 memory caching and read-only S3 sync sidecar]
- Case Management Container -> Database & Storage [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]

## Technology Stack
- Go or Rust: Selected for the fraud scoring engine to eliminate garbage collection pauses and achieve sub-50ms P99 latency.
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Chosen to operate containers without Kubernetes management overhead within budget.
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2: Utilized for scalable transactional and audit data persistence.
- Amazon ElastiCache with Redis OSS: Deployed for low-latency feature lookups and rate limiting.
- MLflow on Amazon ECS: Implemented for zero-downtime model and rule registry management.

## Rationale
This architecture uses memory-safe compiled languages, asynchronous logging, and containerized serverless infrastructure to meet strict sub-50ms latency and high-throughput requirements within budget. Robust fallback mechanisms and automated security controls ensure PCI-DSS compliance and high availability.

Case Management Container.analysis:
## Overview
[Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System screens card-not-present payment authorizations in under 50ms and provides case management for fraud analysts. It maintains PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a strict 7-year tamper-evident audit trail within a €25,000 monthly budget.]

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts & Risk/Compliance Officers [person]
- API Gateway / Ingress Container [container, AWS API Gateway or Envoy]
- Fraud Scoring Engine Container [container, Go or Rust]
- Case Management Container [container, Node.js/Python + React SPA on Amazon S3 / CloudFront]
- Model Registry Container [container, MLflow on Amazon ECS]
- Database & Storage [container, Amazon Aurora Serverless v2]
- Caching Layer [container, Amazon ElastiCache with Redis OSS]
- Case API Router [component, Node.js Express/Fastify]
- Analyst Action Service [component]
- Case Management UI [component, React SPA]
- Case Search & Filter Service [component]
- Batch Processing Coordinator [component]

- Fraud Analysts & Risk/Compliance Officers -> Case Management Container: HTTPS via TLS 1.3
- Case Management UI -> Case API Router: HTTPS via TLS 1.3 (JSON/REST)
- Case API Router -> Analyst Action Service: Internal function calls
- Case API Router -> Case Search & Filter Service: Internal function calls
- Case API Router -> Batch Processing Coordinator: Internal function calls
- Analyst Action Service -> Database & Storage: PostgreSQL Wire Protocol
- Case Search & Filter Service -> Database & Storage: PostgreSQL Wire Protocol
- Batch Processing Coordinator -> Database & Storage: PostgreSQL Wire Protocol

## Technology Stack
- Node.js / Python: Powers the backend API for case management and batch processing efficiently with a 3-person team.
- React SPA on Amazon S3 / CloudFront: Delivers a secure, high-performance analyst interface with strict public-to-private trust boundaries.
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Runs backend containers securely inside private VPC subnets without Kubernetes overhead.
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2: Provides auto-scaling transactional storage with append-only tables and immutable triggers for R-06 auditability.

## Rationale
[This architecture uses managed serverless AWS services and lightweight container runtimes to meet strict sub-50ms performance and PCI-DSS requirements within budget. It empowers a 3-person engineering team to operate the platform reliably while ensuring complete auditability and zero-downtime model updates.]

## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System screens card-not-present payment authorizations in real time to prevent financial fraud while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It evaluates transactions under 50 milliseconds and provides case management tools for fraud analysts.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System [softwareSystem, context]
- Payment Merchants / End Consumers [person, context]
- Fraud Analysts & Risk/Compliance Officers [person, context]
- Risk / Data Scientists [person, context]
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer [externalSystem, context]
- Card Networks / Tokenization Vault [externalSystem, context]
- Identity Provider (IdP) [externalSystem, context]
- API Gateway / Ingress Container (AWS API Gateway or Envoy)
- Fraud Scoring Engine Container (Go or Rust)
- Case Management Container (Node.js/Python + React SPA on Amazon S3 / CloudFront)
- Model Registry Container (MLflow on Amazon ECS)
- Database & Storage (Amazon Aurora Serverless v2)
- Caching Layer (Amazon ElastiCache with Redis OSS)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> API Gateway / Ingress Container (HTTPS / gRPC)
- Fraud Analysts & Risk/Compliance Officers -> Case Management Container (HTTPS via TLS 1.3)
- API Gateway / Ingress Container -> Card Networks / Tokenization Vault (HTTPS via mTLS)
- API Gateway / Ingress Container -> Identity Provider (IdP) (HTTPS via mTLS / OAuth2/SAML)
- API Gateway / Ingress Container -> Fraud Scoring Engine Container (gRPC over AWS VPC internal networks via mTLS)
- Fraud Scoring Engine Container -> Caching Layer (Redis OSS Protocol)
- Fraud Scoring Engine Container -> Database & Storage (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol)
- Case Management Container -> Database & Storage (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol)
- Model Registry Container -> Fraud Scoring Engine Container (S3 memory caching)
- Risk / Data Scientists -> Model Registry Container (HTTPS / AWS IAM)

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Chosen as the target cloud provider to meet infrastructure constraints and latency requirements.
- Go or Rust: Selected for the Fraud Scoring Engine Container to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 requests per second.
- MLflow on Amazon ECS: Implemented for the Model Registry Container to manage zero-downtime model and rule updates.
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2: Utilized for Database & Storage to persist transactional and audit data with append-only tables.
- Amazon ElastiCache with Redis OSS: Deployed as the Caching Layer for low-latency feature lookups and rate limiting.

## Rationale
This serverless-first, containerized architecture fits the requirements by maintaining high availability and sub-50ms performance under peak loads while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS compliance. It ensures robust 7-year auditability and secure cryptographic integrity within a 3-engineer operational model and a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
